column7: Both break-glass revoke entry points (core.RevokeBreakGlass, backing the REST/gRPC human routes, and the /system RevokeBreakGlassActivationProxy) ran role removal and the activation-state update as two independent top-level storage calls, not one transaction -- an effect-then-error fault on RemoveRole (the DELETE lands, the call still reports failure) left the role gone but the activation still "active" and no break_glass.revoked audit event, oracle (d): Differing tables vs before [UserRole], vs reference [BreakGlassActivation AuditEvent]. Fixed by a new shared internal/core.RevokeBreakGlassActivationAtomic wrapping both storage calls in one storage.WithTransaction, called by both entry points; audit/cache-eviction moved to strictly after commit (CreateRole/UpdateRole's #1969/#1996 convention). No SAVEPOINT needed (verified against real Postgres, not just asserted): RemoveRole's tolerated "already gone" case is a zero-rows DELETE, not a genuine aborting SQL statement. Proving test is the fuzz harness itself -- corpus entry 7c0a2492ee5d1dfa is the permanent regression (red-before/green-after confirmed by reverting the fix in the dev worktree and replaying). See docs/findings/2026-09-23-FINDING-breakglass-revoke-half-commit.md. Regression-corpus fidelity note (2026-09-27): ADR-108 Phase 6 step 14c's opCatalog shrink silently retargeted this corpus file's decoded operation from "REST POST /api/v1/roles/" to an unrelated op -- repaired by re-encoding the file's byte[0] to the same op's new index, verified to decode back to the original op/method/NthCall/kind tuple; guarded going forward by TestOpcatalogCorpusFilesTargetPinnedOps (server/faultops/opcatalog_corpus_pin_test.go).
